readings.title: The Covenant of the Parts
readings.text: [Genesis 15:1] After these events <dn>The Word of YeHoVaH</dn> came to Abram in a vision, saying, <dq>“Do not be afraid, Abram. <dn>I</dn> am your shield, your reward is exceedingly great.”</dq> [2] And Abram said, “<dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>, what would <dn>You</dn> give me, seeing I go childless, and the possessor of my house is Eli‛ezer of Damascus?” [3] And Abram said, “See, <dn>You</dn> have given me no seed, and see, one born in my house is my heir!” [4] And see, <dn>The Word of YeHoVaH</dn> came to him, saying, <dq>“This one is not your heir, but he who comes from your own body is your heir.”</dq> [5] And <dn>He</dn> brought him outside and said, <dq>“Look now toward the heavens, and count the stars if you are able to count them.”</dq> And <dn>He</dn> said to him, <dq>“So shall your seed be.”</dq> [6] And he believed in <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, and <dn>He</dn> reckoned it to him for righteousness. [7] And <dn>He</dn> said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>YeHoVaH</dn>, who brought you out of Ur of the Kasdim, to give you this land to inherit it.”</dq> [8] And he said, “<dn>Master YeHoVaH</dn>, whereby do I know that I possess it?” [9] And <dn>He</dn> said to him, <dq>“Bring <dn>Me</dn> a three-year-old heifer, and a three-year-old female goat, and a three-year-old ram, and a turtledove, and a young pigeon.”</dq> [10] And he took all these to <dn>Him</dn> and cut them in the middle, and placed each piece opposite the other, but he did not cut the birds. [11] And the birds of prey came down on the carcasses, and Abram drove them away. [12] And it came to be, when the sun was going down, and a deep sleep fell upon Abram, that see, a horror and great darkness fell upon him. [13] And <dn>He</dn> said to Abram, <dq>“Know for certain that your seed are to be sojourners in a land that is not theirs, and shall serve them, and they shall afflict them four hundred years.</dq> [14] <dq>“But the nation whom they serve <dn>I</dn> am going to judge, and afterward let them come out with great possessions.</dq> [15] <dq>“Now as for you, you are to go to your fathers in peace, you are to be buried at a good old age.</dq> [16] <dq>“And in the fourth generation they return here, for the crookedness of the Amorites is not yet complete.”</dq> [17] And it came to be, when the sun went down and it was dark, that see, a smoking oven and a burning torch that passed between those pieces. [18] On the same day <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> made a covenant with Abram, saying, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> have given this land to your seed, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the River Pharat,</dq> [19] <dq>with the Qénite, and the Qenizzite, and the Qaḏmonite,</dq> [20] <dq>and the Ḥittite, and the Perizzite, and the Repha’im,</dq> [21] <dq>and the Amorite, and the Kena‛anite, and the Girgashite, and the Yebusite.”</dq>

readings.title: Hagar and Ishmael
readings.text: [Genesis 16:1] And Sarai, Abram’s wife, had borne him no children. And she had an Egyptian female servant whose name was Hag̱ar. [2] And Sarai said to Abram, “See now, <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has kept me from bearing children. Please, go in to my female servant, it might be that I am built up by her.” And Abram listened to the voice of Sarai. [3] And Sarai, Abram’s wife, took Hag̱ar her female servant, the Egyptian, and gave her to her husband Abram to be his wife, after Abram had dwelt ten years in the land of Kena‛an. [4] And he went in to Hag̱ar, and she conceived. And when she saw that she had conceived, her mistress was despised in her eyes. [5] And Sarai said to Abram, “My wrong be upon you! I gave my female servant into your bosom. And when she saw that she had conceived, I was despised in her eyes. Let <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> judge between you and me.” [6] And Abram said to Sarai, “See, your female servant is in your hand. Do to her what is good in your eyes.” And Sarai treated her harshly, and she fled from her presence. [7] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> found her by a spring of water in the wilderness, by the spring on the way to Shur, [8] and said, <dq>“Hag̱ar, Sarai’s female servant, where have you come from, and where are you going?”</dq> And she said, “I am fleeing from the presence of my mistress Sarai.” [9] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> said to her, <dq>“Return to your mistress, and humble yourself under her hand.”</dq> [10] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> said to her, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am going to increase your seed greatly, so that it is too numerous to be counted.”</dq> [11] And the <dn>Messenger of YeHoVaH</dn> said to her, <dq>“See, you are pregnant and bearing a son, and shall call his name Yishma‛ĕl, because <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> has heard your affliction.</dq> [12] <dq>“And he is to be a wild man, his hand against every one and every one’s hand against him, and dwell over against all his brothers.”</dq> [13] And she called the Name of <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> who spoke to her, “<dn>You</dn> are the <dn>Ěl</dn> who sees,” for she said, “Have I also here seen <dn>Him</dn> who sees me?” [14] That is why the well was called Be’ĕr Laḥai Ro’i. See, it is between Qaḏesh and Bereḏ. [15] And Hag̱ar bore Abram a son, and Abram called the name of his son, whom Hag̱ar bore, Yishma‛ĕl. [16] And Abram was eighty-six years old when Hag̱ar bore Yishma‛ĕl to Abram.

readings.title: The Covenant of Circumcision
readings.text: [Genesis 17:1] And it came to be when Abram was ninety-nine years old, that <dn>YeHoVaH</dn> appeared to Abram and said to him, <dq>“<dn>I</dn> am <dn>Ěl Shaddai</dn>. Walk before <dn>Me</dn> and be perfect.</dq> [2] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> give <dn>My</dn> covenant between <dn>Me</dn> and you, and increase you exceedingly.”</dq> [3] And Abram fell on his face, and <dn>Elohim</dn> spoke with him, saying, [4] <dq>“As for <dn>Me</dn>, look, <dn>My</dn> covenant is with you, and you shall become a father of many nations.</dq> [5] <dq>“And no longer is your name called Abram, but your name shall be Abraham, for <dn>I</dn> have made you a father of many nations.</dq> [6] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall make you exceedingly fruitful, and make nations of you, and sovereigns shall come from you.</dq> [7] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>My</dn> covenant between <dn>Me</dn> and you and your seed after you in their generations, for an everlasting covenant, to be <dn>Elohim</dn> to you and your seed after you.</dq> [8] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall give to you and your seed after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Kena‛an, as an everlasting possession. And <dn>I</dn> shall be their <dn>Elohim</dn>.”</dq>

readings.title: The Sign of the Covenant
readings.text: [Genesis 17:9] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Abraham, <dq>“As for you, guard <dn>My</dn> covenant, you and your seed after you throughout their generations.</dq> [10] <dq>“This is <dn>My</dn> covenant which you guard between <dn>Me</dn> and you, and your seed after you: Every male child among you is to be circumcised.</dq> [11] <dq>“And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin, and it shall become a sign of the covenant between <dn>Me</dn> and you.</dq> [12] <dq>“And a son of eight days is circumcised by you, every male child in your generations, he who is born in your house or bought with silver from any foreigner who is not of your seed.</dq> [13] <dq>“He who is born in your house, and he who is bought with your silver, has to be circumcised. So shall <dn>My</dn> covenant be in your flesh, for an everlasting covenant.</dq> [14] <dq>“And an uncircumcised male child, who is not circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin, his life shall be cut off from his people – he has broken <dn>My</dn> covenant.”</dq>

readings.title: Sarah's Blessing and Isaac Promised
readings.text: [Genesis 17:15] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said to Abraham, <dq>“As for Sarai your wife, do not call her name Sarai, for Sarah is her name.</dq> [16] <dq>“And <dn>I</dn> shall bless her and also give you a son by her. And <dn>I</dn> shall bless her, and she shall become nations – sovereigns of peoples shall be from her.”</dq> [17] And Abraham fell on his face and laughed, and said in his heart, “Is a child born to a man of a hundred years old? And is Sarah, who is ninety years old, to bear a child?” [18] And Abraham said to <dn>Elohim</dn>, “Oh, let Yishma‛ĕl live before <dn>You</dn>!” [19] And <dn>Elohim</dn> said, <dq>“No, Sarah your wife is truly bearing a son to you, and you shall call his name Yitsḥaq. And <dn>I</dn> shall establish <dn>My</dn> covenant with him for an everlasting covenant, and with his seed after him.</dq> [20] <dq>“And as for Yishma‛ĕl, <dn>I</dn> have heard you. See, <dn>I</dn> shall bless him, and make him fruitful, and increase him exceedingly. He is to beget twelve princes, and <dn>I</dn> shall make him a great nation.</dq> [21] <dq>“But <dn>My</dn> covenant <dn>I</dn> establish with Yitsḥaq, whom Sarah is to bear to you at this set time next year.”</dq> [22] And when <dn>He</dn> had ended speaking with him, <dn>Elohim</dn> went up from Abraham. [23] And Abraham took Yishma‛ĕl his son, and all who were born in his house, and all who were bought with his silver, every male among the men of Abraham’s house, and circumcised the flesh of their foreskins that very same day, as <dn>Elohim</dn> had said to him. [24] And Abraham was ninety-nine years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin. [25] And Yishma‛ĕl his son was thirteen years old when he was circumcised in the flesh of his foreskin. [26] That very same day Abraham was circumcised, and his son Yishma‛ĕl. [27] And all the men of his house, born in the house or bought with silver from a foreigner, were circumcised with him.
